This my millet plot is small, only one-tenth of a hectare, but I want a good harvest because we eat from it. I will put a small amount of fertilizer — I cannot afford much, but a little urea at top-dressing helps the millet tiller well in our sandy soil here in the North West. I will also spread some manure from my animals before the rains come, since that is what my father always did and it keeps the soil from getting tired. I will plant my own saved millet seed like always, and since the plot is small, my family and I can work it ourselves without hiring anyone.
